findings.title: A job-level `if: false` on the release job skips the whole release (npm publish, GitHub Release, GHCR) while the gate stays green
findings.where: scripts/verify-github-workflows.mjs, validateWorkflow() release.yml branch — only step keys are restricted (STEP_KEYS / NPM_PUBLISH_SHAPE_KEYS); job keys are not inspected, so `jobs.release.if` is accepted
findings.why: A copy adding `if: false` under `jobs.release` exits 0 with no issue; at runtime the job is skipped and the workflow run concludes success, which is the same silent-stoppage class the H1 finding was about — one line, no red CI. It is outside the frozen step-level direction (which the repair meets), so it does not reopen H1, but the gate's own purpose ('the release must be effective') is not met at job scope.
findings.direction: Reject a literal `if: false` on the release job (or assert the release job carries no `if`) without banning legitimate job conditions; ship one self-test fixture for it.
findings.scope: residual, outside the frozen closure; recommended follow-up before the v0.7.1 tag

findings.title: Two clauses of the repaired publish rule have no independent self-test control
findings.where: scripts/verify-github-workflows.mjs, runSelfTest() fixtures — no fixture adds a second publish step, and the legacy-token-env fixture is also caught by the denylist, so the env/with clause is never the reason a fixture fails
findings.why: Mutation of a COPY: disabling the `publishSteps.length > 1` check leaves --self-test at 34/34, and emptying NPM_PUBLISH_TOKEN_KEYS (= []) also leaves 34/34. Both clauses work when exercised by my adversarial copies (second publish step -> release-npm-publish; `HARMLESS_NAME: ${{ secrets.SOME_SECRET }}` env -> release-npm-tokenless), but the shipped self-test would not notice their removal — contrary to this repository's 'a green gate must be falsifiable' discipline.
findings.direction: Add one fixture with a second publish step (expect release-npm-publish) and one with an arbitrary-name env on the publish step (expect release-npm-tokenless). 34 -> 36 fixtures.
findings.scope: residual, does not reopen M2: the named controls (order, exact shape, tokenless rule) exist and are load-bearing

declinedToJudge: npmjs Trusted Publisher binding (repo + release.yml filename) — not observable anonymously; recorded INCONCLUSIVE, not a finding.
A real OIDC publish, the signed provenance attestation and the actual v0.7.1 tag — unproven until a real tag run; no tag, credential or publish was performed.
Registry *install* path (`dsh plugin add ... @mpd-dsh/silicon@0.7.0`) — not re-measured; the docs state this bound; it needs a writable HOME/dsh profile.
docker-verify.yml / boot-e2e.yml — unchanged and not re-run; outside this change set.

Legitimate job-level conditions other than a literal `if: false` (e.g. a repository-owner guard) — not judged; banning generic job conditions would be over-strict, so F2 proposes only the literal no-op.
Publish step carrying `working-directory` or `timeout-minutes` — gate accepts it, but the step then fails loudly at runtime (no package.json / timeout); not a silent stoppage.

A second publish step spelled `npm  publish` (double space) — not counted as a publish step, but the duplicate version makes one of the two publishes fail loudly (EEXIST); cannot silently stop publishing.
A multi-job restructure that puts publish in a sibling job — not judged: `collectSteps` flattens jobs, so order could be bypassed only by a visible structural rewrite, not a one-line drift.
Comment lines in release.yml naming NPM_TOKEN/.npmrc — correctly ignored (comments are not semantic values); the real tree passes.
Denylist false-positive risk from the `_auth` substring — no legitimate value currently contains it; a future false positive fails closed and loudly.
Deliberate obfuscation (base64-written .npmrc, NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG) — outside the drift threat model; a structural gate cannot prove absence against an adversary.
Historical CHANGELOG lines that say 'no npm publish' for older releases — history, not a current claim; only the 0.7.0 supersession sentence was in scope and it is now accurate.

Self-test harness asserts passed === total, not a minimum count — deleting a fixture lowers the printed count but keeps exit 0; pre-existing design, which is why the rule-disabling mutation was used as the falsifiability proof.
The previous record's output.log is gitignored (`*.log`), so it cannot be committed as-is; that record was deliberately left untouched and this record uses `output.txt`.
pack-silicon walks the whole tree including gitignored scratch — reviewer scratch at mode 600 tripped `--check` once; pre-existing packer behaviour, not a change-set defect.
bounds: The real GitHub Actions tag run is UNPROVEN: no OIDC token exchange, no npm provenance attestation, no actual v0.7.1 publish (no tag, no credentials). Only the workflow definition, the offline gate and adversarial copies were measured.
The npmjs trusted-publisher binding is UNPROVEN: not exposed anonymously.
Did not run docker-verify.yml or boot-e2e.yml (Docker image build, real harness boots); out of scope for this change set.
Did not run the registry install path end to end (needs a writable HOME/dsh profile).

The adversarial copies live under gitignored .tmp/ and were removed from the verdict evidence; only the recorded outputs are kept. The real .github/** was never written (sha256 identical before/after).

The bun-oracle run used a python3 shim that exits 1 to force the Bun.YAML.parse fallback; both oracles agree (4/4 and 34/34).
verdictJustification: All five findings are closed with observed evidence on adversarial copies — the six publish-shape holes now fail with release-npm-publish while a clean copy passes, legacy token shapes and all eight denylist needles fail with release-npm-tokenless, --self-test is 34/34 with load-bearing controls for order/exact-shape/tokenless, the Unreleased sentence names the real 0.7.0 claim without touching history, and both CONTRIBUTING files say only vX.Y.Z — and the full §3 chain is green; the two remaining findings (job-level `if`, two self-test branches) are non-blocking residuals outside the frozen closure.
